claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element automotive alloy containing multiple elements, including platinum-group metals, in nearly equiatomic ratios.
A conformal, porous CeO2 overlayer can be deposited by atomic layer deposition at approximately 200°C.
The deposited CeO2 film will be thinner than 2 nm.
The coated catalyst will receive a mild air calcination at 300–350°C.
The CeO2 overlayer will form a highly dispersed oxygen-buffering nanolayer.
The CeO2 nanolayer will bond intimately to the alloy surface.
The CeO2 nanolayer will act as a protective shell while enabling oxygen mobility.
The CeO2 overlayer will mitigate catalyst sintering by acting as a physical barrier.
The CeO2 overlayer will mitigate redox-induced structural changes by mediating oxygen storage and release.
Oxygen mediation by the CeO2 overlayer will promote low-temperature oxidation reactions.
The CeO2 overlayer will promote NO reduction reactions.
The overlayer will preserve active alloy sites during transient operation and aging.
Compared with the untreated catalyst, the CeO2-coated catalyst will maintain or improve low-temperature catalytic activity.
Compared with the untreated catalyst, the coated catalyst will have significantly greater durability during exposure to moisture, NO, and thermal cycling.
Compared with the untreated catalyst, the coated catalyst will exhibit less agglomeration of active sites.
The intervention is anticipated to be effective below approximately 500°C under typical exhaust-gas compositions.
The long-term stability of the ultrathin CeO2 layer under continuous redox cycling over extended mileage is uncertain.
The CeO2 overlayer may create interfacial mass-transport limitations.
